additional_info.subject: Incident Report for DC Sicharge D 300 kW Charging Station (MPR8170002536)
additional_info.body:
Hello,
I would like to report an issue with the DC Sicharge D 300 kW charging station (MPR8170002536). Here are the details:
•     Affected connector: Left connector
•     Observed issue: During charging sessions, the process initially starts correctly (green indicator on the truck side). However, after a short time, the connector switches to fault mode with an orange indicator. This issue persists despite cleaning the connector with compressed air.
•     Tests performed: A test was conducted on Thursday, November 14, 2024, between 7:00 PM and 8:00 PM by the fleet trainers. I have also observed similar faults during my own checks.
Despite these actions, the issue remains unresolved.
I kindly request your intervention to identify and resolve this incident. Please keep me informed of the next steps.

additional_info.subject: ID0390475-DC/Si-D/FR[170002536] - DC1 charging issues CRM:00315002071
additional_info.body:
Hello Malek, good morning. I hope you are doing well.
As I mentioned in the previous ticket, let's continue in this one.
I believe I didn't explain it in the previous ticket, when we did the Vehicle Integration for this EV, we noticed that the only way it doesn't work is when we have another EV charging in parallel, it doesn't start the charging session.
All of the 3 trucks that were tested are Volvo FHE which according to our sources, doesn't have an difference in terms of Firmware related to the FME as the difference is supposedly only in architecture (FME is smaller than FHE).
Yesterday, me and Sebastien, with the assistance of Corentin, were able to test 3 trucks in both SiDs from Courthézon location. These are 2 chargers and 3 trucks:
AP1DUJ = Charger 1
tdA3ac = charger 2
EV ID =
0016810ee438 = truck 1
EV ID = 0016810ee656 = truck 2
Truck 3 we weren't able to get the EV ID.
When the colleague arrived on site there was a EV already plugged (Truck 2) in DC2. When we tried to plug in Truck 1 in DC1, it worked in DC1 and DC2, this is the reason why we could get the EV ID.
We tried to plug in Truck 2 again with no success.
We tried Truck 3 and also didn't work in any outlet.
We then moved to the Charger 2 with truck 2 and truck 1. Truck 2 immediately worked in both outlets, which is why we got the 2nd EV ID.
But Truck 1 didn't work in any outlet.
I cannot say why the behaviour was like this from the EV's side but what we saw is that when we plug in the second EV, it doesn't send the SLAC communication (doesn't establish PLC link), we have CP signal since we can see the PilotState A → B2 but afterwards there is no more communication and the session fails.
We could confirm this since we used the Debug tool to check for hardware problems and get the SECC logs.
From hardware's point of view there is no problem with the charger.
From the SECC logs point of view here is what we see:
After this log there is nothing else related to the PLC link, so the charger tried to establish the PLC link but the EV doesn't provide the handshake.
Let me know your thoughts and questions.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0390475-DC/Si-D/FR[170002536] - DC1 charging issues CRM:00315002071
additional_info.body:
Bonjour Thomas,
Je te partage une analyse réalisée chez TER Transports suite à un phénomène signalé par Corentin. Lorsqu’un 2ème camion se branche, la session de recharge ne se lance pas.
Après investigation, il ressort que 2 véhicules testés ne réalisent pas le
handshake
. Selon l’équipe R&D de Siemens, le problème serait lié à la communication SLAC, qui ne s’établit pas correctement. Cette communication est essentielle, car elle garantit que le véhicule électrique et la station de recharge sont physiquement connectés.
N’hésite pas à me faire savoir si tu as besoin de plus de détails ou si tu souhaites qu’on en discute davantage.

additional_info.subject: ID0390475-DC/Si-D/FR[170002536] - DC1 charging issues CRM:00315002071
additional_info.body:
Hi Sebastien, good afternoon.
I will assign this ticket to you since the customer is under discussion with Volvo. I will send here a copy of the last email I sent regarding this topic for documentation:
The replies that Volvo send are coming to the ticket but nothing pertinent so far.
There are two open topics that need to be addressed.
One is the BCB wake up function that is only released in CW8 2025 v6.1.X. This one there is really not much we can do, I’ve discussed with Product Champion about this topic and there is not even a test version for us to trial.
The second topic where we worked on it last week with the Volvos, I have nothing to say besides waiting for them, here is the link to the Vehicle Integration performed by Catalina and Ingo on Germany with 2 different customers:
https://siemens.sharepoint.com/teams/eMobilityServiceCollaboration/Lists/Vehicle%20Integration%20Services/VI_Services_List_SiD.aspx
You can download this yourself and see that there was no problem there. Besides a small issue with the
end session
, not the beginning or mid session.
Remember that you cannot share the document with the customer directly, this is for internal use only. But you can share the ideas.
If you are facing several issues with the Volvos, you can also request a Vehicle Integration, this way it would speed up the process between us and Siemens as the colleagues already talk with them.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
